episode.title: Refresh credential-scoped model metadata before starting turns
episode.before: At parent commit 8003609cc703dbf014159055e63a684901855edc, creation of user turns and mailbox-triggered turns did not ask the model manager to reconcile its in-memory catalog with the currently resolved credentials. A shared catalog could therefore retain metadata fetched for another identity, while turn construction consumed bundled or stale capability metadata. The manager interface had no dedicated best-effort operation for this transition.
episode.after: At commit 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d, the model manager exposes a best-effort credential-change refresh. It resolves lazy credentials before comparing identities, skips static or already-matching catalogs, otherwise reuses a matching cached catalog or fetches online, and bounds authentication plus cache/fetch work with a five-second deadline while retaining existing fallback metadata on failure. User-turn construction and mailbox-triggered wakeups invoke this reconciliation before constructing turn metadata; mailbox wakeups also recheck that their reserved active turn is still current after the asynchronous discovery wait.
episode.diff: The commit modifies five files with 291 insertions and 2 deletions. It adds the refresh contract and implementation to the model-catalog manager, calls it from the user-turn and mailbox-wakeup entry paths, adds a post-refresh mailbox reservation check, expands command-auth coverage to prove lazy credential resolution precedes identity comparison, and adds parameterized integration coverage for successful refresh, discovery failure, and authentication timeout across user and mailbox turn triggers.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d resolves issue/PR 46508 and identifies parent 8003609cc703dbf014159055e63a684901855edc; its stated problem is that credential changes can leave the in-memory model catalog associated with another identity.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0], parent_commit, and commit_show_stat; git show --format=fuller 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d

evidence_units.claim: The parent user-turn construction path applied turn settings and immediately activated environments and built the turn context; the change inserts catalog reconciliation before those operations, except for basic guardian session sources.

The parent mailbox-triggered wakeup path reserved an active turn and immediately consumed queued input; the change inserts catalog reconciliation and then verifies that the same turn reservation remains active before proceeding.
evidence_units.source: git diff 8003609cc703dbf014159055e63a684901855edc 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d -- codex-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs; added lines around 460-473

evidence_units.claim: The manager interface gains a default no-op credential-change refresh, allowing static or alternate catalog implementations to require no refresh while preserving interface compatibility.

The dynamic catalog implementation resolves lazy credentials through should_refresh_models before reading the endpoint identity, returns without network work for a non-refreshable or identity-matching catalog, and otherwise calls refresh_available_models with OnlineIfUncached.
Authentication resolution and catalog cache/fetch access are enclosed in a five-second timeout; failures and timeouts only emit a warning, leaving the existing cache or bundled fallback available.
evidence_units.source: git show 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d:codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs, timeout and warning around lines 379-386; method documentation around lines 138-149

evidence_units.claim: A non-basic user turn passes the effective turn configuration's HTTP client factory to catalog reconciliation before turn environments and context are created.
A mailbox-triggered wakeup passes the current session HTTP client factory to catalog reconciliation before reading pending input and constructing its turn.

After mailbox discovery completes, the wakeup compares its saved turn-state pointer with the current active turn and returns if the reservation was removed or replaced, preventing an interrupted wakeup from continuing.

The parameterized integration test covers user success, user discovery failure, mailbox success, mailbox discovery failure, and user authentication timeout after rotating away from and back to an identity whose shared catalog was replaced.
evidence_units.source: git show 2b842962883f2e01526b9c64e383cb2375123a5d:codex-rs/core/tests/suite/models_cache_auth.rs, test cases and auth_rotation_refreshes_before_turn_with_best_effort around lines 103-215

evidence_units.claim: The integration test proves successful discovery changes the TurnStarted context window and capability-derived request shape, while failure or timeout preserves bundled fallback metadata; all cases still send the turn using the rotated authorization credential and complete normally.

The command-auth test explicitly invokes credential-change reconciliation while the previously cached identity still matches and verifies that resolving the next lazy token triggers an additional catalog request; expected request credentials change from two requests to three.
The implementation-bearing change modifies the catalog manager, both relevant turn-start call sites, and two test locations, totaling five changed files.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile_credential_scoped_catalog
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile cached capability metadata with the active credentials
candidate_atomics.description: Before metadata is consumed for new work, resolve the active credential identity and refresh only when the dynamic in-memory catalog belongs to a different identity, using cache-aware online discovery under a bounded best-effort deadline.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a new operation from using capability and limit metadata associated with a previously active identity without making metadata discovery a hard availability dependency.
semantic_action.pre_state: A dynamic in-memory capability catalog may have been populated under credentials different from the lazily resolved credentials that will authorize the next operation.
semantic_action.post_state: Before capability metadata is consumed, the catalog either matches the resolved active identity or the prior cache/bundled fallback remains usable because discovery failed or exceeded its deadline; static catalogs remain unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Rotate the credential source after another identity has replaced the shared catalog. Assert that successful discovery changes context-window and capability-derived request behavior, that failure or authentication timeout retains fallback metadata without blocking the operation, and that lazy command credentials are resolved before identity comparison.

candidate_atomics.name: gate_turn_metadata_on_catalog_reconciliation
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile capability metadata before constructing a turn
candidate_atomics.description: Place credential-aware catalog reconciliation on each applicable turn-start path before the turn captures context limits and capability flags.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure user-initiated and queued-wakeup turns derive their context limits and request capabilities from metadata reconciled with the credentials used for that turn.
semantic_action.pre_state: A user input or trigger-bearing queued message is ready to start a turn, but the shared catalog may still describe another credential identity.
semantic_action.post_state: Every applicable user or mailbox turn attempts catalog reconciliation before its turn context captures capability metadata; excluded basic session sources preserve their existing path.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise both user and mailbox triggers after credential rotation. Observe TurnStarted metadata and the emitted request to prove reconciliation precedes turn construction, while discovery failures and timeouts still allow completion with fallback metadata.

candidate_atomics.name: revalidate_async_wakeup_ownership
candidate_atomics.title: Revalidate wakeup ownership after asynchronous discovery
candidate_atomics.description: After a queued-work wakeup waits for catalog discovery, verify that its reserved active-turn state is still current before consuming input or starting work.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an interrupted or superseded queued-work wakeup from continuing to start a turn after an asynchronous preflight wait.
semantic_action.pre_state: A wakeup has reserved an active-turn state and then awaited credential and catalog discovery, during which cancellation or replacement may change the active turn.
semantic_action.post_state: The wakeup continues only if the current active-turn state is pointer-identical to its saved reservation; otherwise it returns before consuming queued input or constructing a turn.
semantic_action.validation: At the post-discovery boundary, compare the saved reservation with the currently active turn and require early return on absence or replacement. The checked-in implementation provides this guard; a dedicated interruption race test is not present in the changed tests.

candidate_workflows.name: refresh_identity_bound_capabilities_before_turns
candidate_workflows.title: Refresh identity-bound capability metadata before starting turns
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for systems where shared capability metadata can outlive credential changes: establish a bounded, cache-aware reconciliation operation, invoke it before every applicable turn captures metadata, and revalidate ownership when an asynchronous wakeup can be interrupted.

workflow_graph.goal: Start each applicable turn with capability metadata belonging to the credentials that authorize it, while preserving turn availability when catalog discovery is unavailable or slow.
when_to_use: Capability or model metadata is cached in memory and scoped, directly or indirectly, to an authenticated identity.
Credentials can rotate, be lazily resolved, or be shared across multiple turn-start paths while the process remains alive.
Turn construction consumes catalog fields such as context limits or request capability flags.
anti_goals: Do not make remote catalog discovery a mandatory condition for starting a turn.
Do not unconditionally fetch the catalog when static metadata is used or the resolved identity already matches the cached entry.
Do not refresh after the turn context has already captured capability metadata.
Do not let an interrupted queued-work wakeup resume merely because asynchronous discovery completed.
not_applicable_when: Capability metadata is immutable and independent of credentials for the lifetime of the process.
Every credential change creates a new isolated catalog owner and no metadata is shared across identities.
The operation being started does not consume identity-dependent catalog or capability metadata.
inputs: A credential resolver capable of yielding the identity used by the next request
The identity associated with the current in-memory catalog
A cache-aware catalog refresh operation and HTTP client factory
The complete set of applicable user and queued-work turn-start paths
For interruptible wakeups, a stable reservation token or turn-state identity
workflow_graph.entry_state: A turn trigger is ready, but the process may hold capability metadata obtained for a different or not-yet-resolved credential identity.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The applicable turn captures metadata after a bounded reconciliation attempt, uses refreshed metadata on success or the existing fallback on failure, and an interruptible wakeup proceeds only while it still owns the active-turn reservation.

steps.condition: The catalog implementation is dynamic and may be identity-scoped.
steps.validation: Confirm lazy credentials are resolved before identity comparison, matching identities avoid a fetch, mismatches use cache-aware online discovery, and the whole attempt has a bounded best-effort deadline.

steps.condition: Apply to every turn-start path that consumes identity-dependent metadata; retain explicit exclusions for paths whose lifecycle must not refresh.
steps.validation: For both direct user input and trigger-bearing queued input, verify reconciliation occurs before the turn reports its context window or constructs capability-dependent request fields.

steps.condition: Required when a turn-start path reserves mutable lifecycle state before awaiting reconciliation and can be cancelled or superseded during that wait.
steps.validation: After the wait, require the saved reservation to equal the current active state and return before input consumption when it does not.

validation_ladder: Unit/integration-test lazy credential rotation to prove identity comparison uses newly resolved credentials rather than the previously cached identity.
Test successful refresh after another identity replaces the shared catalog; assert turn-visible limits and capability-derived request fields use the discovered metadata.
Test discovery failure and credential-resolution timeout; assert the turn starts within the deadline and uses existing bundled or cached fallback metadata.
Exercise every applicable trigger path, including direct user input and queued mailbox wakeups, and assert the request uses the active credential.
Add a focused cancellation or replacement race test for the post-discovery wakeup ownership check.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the catalog entry has no observable identity association and mismatch cannot be established safely.
Stop if no bounded fallback exists and adding best-effort discovery would silently weaken a required hard-failure contract.
Stop if an applicable turn-start path cannot be identified before capability metadata is captured.
Do not claim complete race validation until the interrupted-wakeup ownership branch has a dedicated test oracle.
unresolved_or_deferred: The changed tests do not directly force cancellation or replacement of a mailbox wakeup during discovery, so the ownership recheck is implementation-grounded but lacks a dedicated race test.
Repository metadata does not include PR review discussion or status-check results, and no test suite was executed as part of this extraction.

unresolved_questions: Was the post-discovery mailbox ownership branch covered by an unchanged test elsewhere or by external CI? No direct test for that race was found in the changed files or supplied GitHub bundle.

Which exact basic guardian session-source invariant justifies excluding that user-turn path from refresh? The exclusion is explicit in implementation, but its rationale is not established by the supplied evidence.
